text:
Lawson Crouse is doing a lot of the work for Utah and getting little of the credit. He has 63 hits, and Utah takes 57% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on (expected goals measure the quality of chances). But he has two goals in 24 games on 5.5 expected, and the team has scored about four fewer goals than its chances with him on the ice.

That is a slump in the finish, not the process. Crouse scored 24 last season, and Evolving-Hockey had most of his value at even strength. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows a surprising touch: 18% of his setups go across the royal road, the pass that moves a goalie side to side, against 7% for a typical forward. He has spent his whole career with this franchise, from Arizona to Utah. Our range has him around 16 goals. When the goals start, they should come in bunches.
